valuation.method: Forward adjusted EPS x P/E. FY2027 adjusted EPS per share, viewed at the 12-month target date (November 2027), x a P/E applied to that earnings period. Listing: TTE on the NYSE has been the ordinary share since 8 December 2025, when the ADR program terminated; the TotalEnergies FAQ states 1 ADR = 1 NYSE ordinary share, so the ratio is 1:1 and no ratio conversion is applied. The US-market depositary per the FAQ is DTC. TotalEnergies reports in USD (financial currency USD), so model EPS and targets need no FX conversion. Analyst targets that the aggregator shows in USD but that are round euro amounts (UBS, RBC, Citi, Bank of America, Jefferies, DBS, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Barclays) were converted at the Banque de France euro reference rate of 1.1052 USD per EUR for 13 November 2026, the reference close date. The EUR originals (93, 90, 95, 89, 90, 87, 85, 82, 100, 95) are inferred by dividing the TipRanks USD figures by 1.0994, which reproduces integers exactly; the original euro notes were not opened. Targets are price-only; dividends are excluded and dividend_per_share is null. Base EPS $10.50 is a model assumption: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $4.03 at Brent $97/b and a European refining margin marker of $33.2/b, against Q2 2026 at $2.68 with Brent $103.8/b and a margin of $13.5/b, so FY2027 is set below the Q3 run-rate on partial normalisation of refining margins and gas prices.

bear.driver: Refining margin and gas/LNG prices revert toward mid-cycle; Brent falls back to about $60/b; buybacks continue at a slower pace

base.driver: Partial normalisation of the Q3 2026 refining and gas tailwind; Brent averaging about $85/b in 2027; production growth above 3% per year toward the 2030 target; $2.5bn of buybacks for Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 maintained

bull.driver: Oil and gas prices stay near the Q3 2026 and early Q4 2026 levels (the company says oil remains above $100/b at the start of Q4) through 2027, with refining margins holding and the share count falling faster

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS of $10.50 the close of $90.74 implies 8.6x. The equal-weight mean of the 13 named analyst targets dated on or before the 13 November close ($99.91, median $99.47) implies about 9.5x at base EPS, or about $11.10 of EPS at 9.0x (about 6% above the base case).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base EPS of $10.50 moves the base target by $10.50 (11.6 pp of the close). A $1.00 change in FY2027 EPS moves the base target by $9.00 at 9.0x (9.9 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted EPS per share and the European refining margin marker. The base case needs FY2027 adjusted EPS near $10.50, i.e. about $2.63 per quarter against Q3 2026's $4.03, so it assumes the refining margin stays well above its Q2 2026 level. A sustained fall of the margin marker toward $13.5/b, or Brent falling below about $75/b, would move the case toward the bear.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results, with 2027 guidance, expected in early 2027. The exact date is not confirmed in the sources reviewed, and the company has not provided a 2027 outlook in the Q3 2026 release.

analyst_notes: Fourteen named analysts with dated calls on or before the 13 November close: ten Buy and four Hold, with 27 events in total (13 targets and 14 ratings; DZ Bank has a rating only). Targets range from $91.00 (Freedom Capital Markets, raised from $81) to $110.52 (Barclays, raised from $104.99 on 4 October). The equal-weight mean is $99.91 and the median $99.47, about 10% and 9.6% above the close. Six events post-date the 29 October Q3 release (UBS, RBC, Freedom, Citi, Bank of America and DZ Bank's rating) and three are dated that day (Jefferies, DBS, Piper Sandler). The four priors we have (Citi, Freedom, Goldman Sachs, Barclays) all show raises, and the euro priors are converted at the same rate as the current targets, so each comparison is like for like. The gap to the base case of $94.50 is best explained by the earnings path, since the mean implies about $11.10 of EPS at 9.0x against the $10.50 base. None of these calls states a 12-month horizon for the individual broker, so horizon_months is null and none enters a weighted target. A Kepler Capital upgrade to Buy dated 17 November 2026 is excluded because it post-dates the reference close. The Q3 release time is not confirmed in the sources reviewed; the 29 October date comes from the company's release and the time shown is an assumed Paris morning. Coverage is partial.
